messages.author: 5f4538afa2f74b06
messages.subject: mdm
parts:
Hello everyone,

I come with a simple question. I'm starting to run a new analysis, and I found that "mdm"  &"mmdm" (and in consequence sigma) take very low values (<80m).

                      S1
n individuals 14
n traps 63
n occasions 37
                     S1
avg caps 2.50
avg spatial caps 1.86
mmdm 0.05

Here my scrFrame:
str(sf, max.level = 1) List of 11
$ caphist :List of 1
$ traps :List of 1
$ indCovs :List of 1
$ trapCovs : NULL
$ sigCovs :'data.frame': 1 obs. of 1 variable:
$ trapOperation:List of 1
$ occasions : int 37
$ type : chr "scr"
$ mmdm : num 0.0483
$ mdm : num 0.0801
$ telemetry : NULL - attr(*, "class")= chr "scrFrame"

...and the spider plot attached.

The low values could be explained as a consequence of the fact that for most animals I don't have spatial recaptures? And furthermore, due to the low number of spatial recaptures, are these data not appropriate for an SCR analysis?

As some of the animals (e.g. purple, brown and yellow on the bottom of the picture) have captured in traps spaced 3-4 Km; I'm not sure if low movement rates are an error (maybe coordinates system?), or are correct, and a consequence of the low spatial recaptures of my animals.

Ps: I'm analysing red deer data on north Europe

Thank you very much
Pablo

parts:
Hi Pablo,

This definitely seems like an error in the coordinates. Can you post the ranges of the trap X and Y values, and/or a simple plot of the X and Y coordinates? Did you attempt to scale the coordinates?

Good news is that the spider pot suggests plenty of spatial recaptures.

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: [oscr] mdm
parts:
﻿Okay, I would double check your coordinates. Looks like they are measured in 100s of kilometers (19.60 to 19.85 is 0.25 units).

Scaling the UTMs from meters to km is often done to reduce the magnitude of the sigma estimate to help with optimizing the maximum likelihood. Maybe these were inadvertently scaled twice?
